title: DITA 1.3 copy-to and chunk output naming
content: Normative DITA 1.3 behavior for copy-to combined with chunking: chunk="to-content" selects the topics referenced by that topicref and its child topicrefs and renders them as one output chunk. When copy-to is specified for that chunk, the output resource name MUST be taken from the copy-to value. This naming rule is verified by the DITA specification; an answer must not label the copy-to/chunk naming interaction as wholly unverified. Topic hierarchy is preserved in the combined chunk, but the specification does not require an AEM-specific JCR layout or a particular HTML section structure.
summary: For a DITA 1.3 chunk with copy-to, the output resource name comes from copy-to; to-content combines the selected topic hierarchy into one output chunk.
learned_behavior: Assert copy-to naming precedence as normative while keeping rendered structure and AEM mappings implementation-specific.
expected_behavior: to-content combines selected topics into one chunk
copy-to supplies the chunk resource name
qa_oracles: Use a unique copy-to filename and verify it names the generated chunk in an output format that supports chunking
risk_signals: assuming a specific HTML or JCR structure
confidence_contract: Normative for DITA 1.3; exact processor output still requires runtime evidence.

title: DITA 1.3 by-topic fixture design
content: A valid by-topic test must use a single physical DITA source document that contains a root topic and one or more nested topics. Reference that document from the map with chunk="by-topic" and verify that a supporting processor splits the nested topics into separate output resources. A map containing only separate sibling or child topicref elements that each point to different physical topic files does not prove by-topic splitting. For the paired to-content case, use a topicref with copy-to="combined.dita" and chunk="to-content" plus child topicrefs, then verify one combined output resource named from combined.dita when the selected transform supports chunking.
summary: A by-topic oracle needs nested topics in one source document; separate topicref targets do not demonstrate splitting.
learned_behavior: Reject fixtures that claim to test by-topic without a multi-topic source document.
expected_behavior: by-topic separates nested topics when supported
to-content combines selected topics when supported
qa_oracles: Count generated resources and verify rewritten navigation against actual processor output
risk_signals: using separate physical topics as the only by-topic fixture
confidence_contract: Normative fixture semantics; observed filenames and links require processor execution.

title: DITA 1.3 copy-to and chunk boundaries
content: Chunk processing is output-format specific and implementation specific. Some transforms can ignore chunking when source-document organization does not affect the result, so the same behavior must not be asserted automatically for AEM Sites, HTML5, and a single-file PDF. The chunk attribute does not cascade from a container topicref to descendant topicrefs. Supplying multiple tokens from the same chunk category is an error. If generated resource names clash, a processor MAY recover by creating alternate resource identifiers; this normative recovery allowance is known, but the exact DITA-OT filename or diagnostic is runtime-specific. The copy-to attribute is not supported when the effective scope is peer or external.
summary: Chunking is transform-specific; non-cascading, conflicting tokens, name collisions, and peer/external copy-to are explicit boundary cases.
learned_behavior: Do not generalize chunk output across formats; include supported negative and portability tests.
expected_behavior: chunk behavior can differ by transform
processors may recover from output-name collisions
qa_oracles: Run each requested transform rather than extrapolating one result
verify peer and external copy-to are rejected or unsupported
risk_signals: claiming identical Sites HTML5 and PDF output
confidence_contract: Normative boundaries; exact DITA-OT and AEM behavior requires versioned runtime evidence.

title: copy-to and chunk evidence contract
content: Evidence contract for answers about copy-to plus chunking. Verified from the DITA 1.3 specification: copy-to gives an alternate resource name for a referenced instance; links and navigation for that instance point to the alternate resource; to-content combines selected topics; copy-to supplies the chunk resource name; chunk support varies by output and implementation; and collision recovery is permitted. Require generated DITA-OT evidence for exact output filenames, temporary preprocessing order, rewritten href values, warnings, and version differences. Require AEM Guides product documentation, code, or live output for AEM Sites paths, JCR properties, workflow behavior, and UI behavior. XML catalog configuration is not a demonstrated dependency of copy-to plus chunking merely because both occur in DITA processing.
summary: Keep specification rules, generated DITA-OT observations, and AEM Guides mappings in separate evidence tiers.
learned_behavior: Answer known specification rules directly and reserve unverified labels for processor- or product-specific results.
workflow_cues: generate output when exact oracle is requested
expected_behavior: normative facts are stated as verified
runtime and product claims remain bounded
qa_oracles: Use generate_dita_ot_output for exact PDF or HTML5 observations when available
risk_signals: using generic XML catalog guidance as feature evidence
confidence_contract: Normative facts are high confidence; implementation observations remain explicitly unverified until generated.
